subject: PGVector + S3 connector — joint pilot & integration roadmap
messages:
From: Alex Chen (PGVector Maintainers) <alex@pgvector.org>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@pinecone.io
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: PGVector + Redwood — S3-backed connector proposal

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well — I’m Alex, one of the maintainers on PGVector. We’ve seen a number of teams building hybrid persistence layers (S3 for cold storage + vector index for hot retrieval) and thought Redwood Inference would be a great partner to support an official PGVector+S3 connector pattern.

High level: we’d like to collaborate on a small pilot that demonstrates:
- seamless write-through from Redwood embeddings -> pgvector index (hot) + S3 (cold)
- automatic rehydration for long-context recovery
- simple operational playbooks for backup and retention across accounts

I attached a short proposal with an architecture sketch and cost assumptions. Would Redwood be open to a 6-week joint pilot with a co-branded integration sample and an ops runbook?

A few questions off the bat:
1) Do you have preferred S3-compatible patterns (single-bucket per-customer vs namespace folders)?
2) Any constraints on embedding formats we should follow?
3) Who on your side would own commercial conversations (for eventual marketplace listing)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min intro next week.

Best,
Alex Chen
PGVector Maintainers
[Attachment: pgvector-s3-connector-proposal.pdf (PDF, 540KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen (PGVector Maintainers) <alex@pgvector.org>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PGVector + Redwood — S3-backed connector proposal

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the proposal. This is squarely in our integrations roadmap and we’d love to run the pilot.

Quick answers:
- We generally recommend a per-customer prefix inside a single bucket (easier lifecycle and cross-account exports), but can support single-bucket-per-customer if partners need strict isolation.
- Embedding format: float32 array is our default, but we frequently work with 8-bit quantized arrays for storage. If you provide both schemas we can support either.
- Commercial lead: looping in Aditya (cc) to handle marketplace listing and term discussions; Vivek will own technical scoping and the pilot plan.

Next steps I propose:
1) 30-min technical kickoff the week of May 11 — Vivek to run it.
2) Share a short PSA + security questionnaire pre-kickoff.
3) Confirm pilot success metrics (latency for 1k qps, cost per 10k tokens, rehydration time under 2s for 90th percentile).

Can you share availability for the kickoff and attach any existing integration guides?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

[Signature]

From: Alex Chen (PGVector Maintainers) <alex@pgvector.org>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PGVector + Redwood — S3-backed connector proposal

Thanks Marissa — available May 12–14 afternoons PT. Sharing the repo and an integration doc here: https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector-s3-connector

Attachment list:
- pgvector-integration-arch.md (architecture notes)
- partnership-term-sheet-v1.docx (draft commercial terms)

Key technical notes:
- We’ll implement a write-through adapter that writes embeddings to pgvector and asynchronously persists a compressed parquet blob to S3 (namespace prefix).
- Rehydration will use an object metadata index to find candidates within a namespace and then stream the parquet content back into the KV cache.
- We’ve mocked up a minimal compatibility shim for 8-bit quantized arrays; full float32 path is the default.

If the term sheet is acceptable we can run the pilot under an MOU; otherwise we can do an initial tech-only POC.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

—Alex
[Attachments: pgvector-integration-arch.md, partnership-term-sheet-v1.docx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Alex — that works. Vivek and I propose May 13 at 2:00pm PT for a 30-min kickoff; Aditya will cover commercial next steps.

Before the call: could you complete our security questionnaire (I’m attaching the template) and share any SOC2/attestation notes if you have them? We’ll also send our standard partner MOU for review.

Onwards: Vivek — can you draft the pilot plan (2-week POC + 4-week validation with success metrics) and share a sample dataset/cost model?

Thanks — see you on the 13th.

Best,
Marissa
